plain.text: There was a famine, and Isaac went to Gerar. The LORD appeared to him: "Do not go down to Egypt. Stay in this land, and I will be with you and bless you." God confirmed to Isaac the promise he had made to Abraham: his descendants would be as many as the stars, they would have the land, and through his offspring all nations would be blessed.

Like his father before him, Isaac was afraid the men of Gerar would kill him because of his beautiful wife, so he said Rebekah was his sister. King Abimelech later saw Isaac and Rebekah together and realised they were married. He scolded Isaac and ordered that no one should harm them.

Isaac planted crops and reaped a hundred times what he sowed, because the LORD blessed him. He became very wealthy, and the Philistines envied him. They filled in the wells his father had dug, and Abimelech asked him to move away. Isaac reopened his father's wells. When local herders quarrelled over two new wells, he moved on and dug another, which no one disputed. He named it Rehoboth ("room"), saying, "The LORD has given us room." At Beersheba the LORD appeared to him: "Do not be afraid, for I am with you." Isaac built an altar there.

Abimelech came with his advisers. Isaac asked why they had come after sending him away. They said, "We can plainly see that the LORD has been with you," and asked for a peace treaty. Isaac made them a feast, they swore an oath, and they left in peace. That day Isaac's servants found water in a new well.
When Esau was forty, he married two Hittite women, and they made life bitter for Isaac and Rebekah.

summary.bigIdea: God renews his promise to Isaac and blesses him, and Isaac chooses peace instead of fighting over wells.
points: God repeats to Isaac the promise he made to Abraham.
Isaac repeats his father's fearful lie, but God protects them.
When others fight over wells, Isaac moves on, and God gives him room.
summary.reflection: Isaac kept moving on rather than fighting. When is it wise to let go of a quarrel?
